verification.factCheck: I fetched core/vm/evm.go from the master branch of bnb-chain/bsc. isSystemCall at lines 291 to 293 compares the caller with params.SystemAddress, which params/protocol_params.go line 238 sets to 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe. EVM.Call skips CanTransfer at line 314 and skips Transfer at lines 345 to 347 for that caller and still passes the value to the callee contract. CallCode (line 409) and create (line 552) keep the balance check for every caller. I repeated the probe on all 21 endpoints of networks.json on 2026-11-23: eth_call from the system address with value 7, a sender balance of 1000 set by state override, to a 16 byte probe that returns CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE and BALANCE(CALLER), probe balance 10. BNB Smart Chain (Geth/v1.8.2-4e1c8247-20261104, near block 135,178,626) returned 7, 10 and 1000 in 12 of 12 runs. The same call from an ordinary address returned 7, 17 and 993 there. Nineteen other endpoints returned 7, 17 and 993 for the system address, and Tempo rejected the call with 'value transfer not allowed'. The system address has no code, nonce 0 and balance 0 on BNB Smart Chain. I looked for every use of the address as a caller in the client. core/state_processor.go builds three messages with From params.SystemAddress (lines 353, 380 and 420) and each evm.Call passes common.U2560 as value to a fixed target. consensus/parlia/parlia.go calls getSystemMessage five times (lines 1389, 2069, 2096, 2110 and 2131) and feynmanfork.go twice (lines 54 and 125), always with header.Coinbase as sender. core/state_transition.go lines 702 and 708 only add fees to the address, and distributeIncoming (parlia.go lines 2022 to 2052) moves that balance to the coinbase. The Jenner stateful precompile entry (core/vm/contracts_stateful.go lines 161 to 186) and the CAS20 prologue (core/vm/cas20.go lines 89 to 95) make no outbound call and reject value. A frame whose address is the system address would need code at that address, an EIP-7702 authorization signed for it, or a transaction signed for it. None of these is open to an ordinary account. go-ethereum master (lines 268 to 309), op-geth on the optimism branch (lines 247 to 304) and the head of celo-org/op-geth (lines 264 to 321) hold the same rule. Bor master (lines 326 and 357), the Nitro fork of go-ethereum (lines 264 and 294) and libevm (lines 196 and 219) check and transfer for every caller. go-ethereum's own three system calls pass value zero (core/state_processor.go lines 387 to 487). eth_call of settle() (0x11da60b4) and settleFor(address) (0x3dd45adb) with value 1 from the system address returned 0x54e3ca0d on BNB Smart Chain and on the other endpoints I ran with both selectors (Ethereum, Unichain, Celo, HyperEVM). settle() returned 0x54e3ca0d on 20 endpoints and Tempo rejected the value. eth_getBalance of the BNB Smart Chain PoolManager returned 3,793.5 BNB. The Jenner date is confirmed: params/config.go line 256 sets JennerTime to 1796697000 and the v1.8.2 release notes give 2026-12-08 02:30 UTC. Not confirmed by me: the revm and Monad source lines the finding names for the other clients. Their endpoints behaved as on Ethereum in the probe.
verification.codeCheck: settle and settleFor are the only payable functions in src (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307). Both carry onlyWhenUnlocked, which reverts with ManagerLocked unless Lock.isUnlocked() is true (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99). _settle credits paid = msg.value to the recipient when the synced currency is address(0) and reads no balance on that branch (src/PoolManager.sol:349-354 and 364). sync(address(0)) stores no reserves (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283). A native credit can be spent by take, which sends value with call(gas(), to, amount, 0, 0, 0, 0) (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). So a frame at the PoolManager that reports a value nobody paid would give a real credit, as the finding says. The guards hold for the case at hand. The unlock flag is set only inside unlock, which then calls unlockCallback on msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). A call that starts from the system address begins with the manager locked, and an account without code cannot run a callback. The PoolManager makes three raw calls. The token transfer and the hook call pass value 0 (src/types/Currency.sol:73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and the native payout uses the PoolManager as caller (src/types/Currency.sol:48), so the PoolManager never calls as the system address. A contract called by the system address with a stated value receives no balance on BNB Smart Chain, so any onward value call to settle would be paid from that contract's own balance. No path from an ordinary account to a native credit follows from this rule.
verification.corrections: The mechanism text says the settle and settleFor probe returned ManagerLocked on all 21 networks. On Tempo the endpoint rejects any call that carries value with 'value transfer not allowed', also when the sender balance is set by override, so the count is 20 and one rejection. With value 0 the Tempo PoolManager returns ManagerLocked. The op-geth line range begins at 247 and the Celo range at 264, where isSystemCall is defined. forno.celo.org answered from two client families during my runs (reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb and Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817) and both moved value for the system address in 12 of 12 runs. The actor value governance and the severity info are right: no party can trigger the hazard today and it needs a consensus rule change.
